title: Central Italian Grapes and Terroir
quiz.0.question: How long can Verdicchio age?
quiz.0.explanation: Top Verdicchio (especially Matelica Riserva) has remarkable ageing potential of 10-20 years, developing complex notes of beeswax, hazelnut and truffle.
quiz.1.question: What is the main grape of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG?
quiz.1.explanation: A common confusion! Vino Nobile di Montepulciano (from a Tuscan town) is made mainly from Sangiovese (locally Prugnolo Gentile), not the Montepulciano grape.
quiz.2.question: Why is Sagrantino's tannin so high?
quiz.2.options.1: Very thick skins and high polyphenol content
quiz.2.explanation: Sagrantino is considered one of the most tannic grapes in the world, thanks to very thick skins and high polyphenol content, plus the traditional long maceration.
quiz.3.question: Why is Pecorino called that?
quiz.3.options.1: Sheep love eating the grapes / sheep migration routes
quiz.3.explanation: Pecorino ("little sheep") has two explanations: sheep love eating the grapes, or Marche and Abruzzo lay on the traditional sheep migration routes (transumanza).

slides.2.title: ⚪ Verdicchio — Grape Profile and Two Key Areas
slides.2.content:
The underrated king of white grapes (from verde = green), Marche's star variety — one of Italy's finest white grapes, with top wines able to age 10-20 years, often likened to "Italy's Chablis"

📊

Grape Profile

Acidity: high to very high

Body: medium to full

Alcohol: 12-14%

Flavours (young): lemon, green apple, white flowers, almond, minerality

Flavours (aged): honey, hazelnut, toasted almond, beeswax, wet stone

Character: high acid + minerality; with age it rivals top white Burgundy

🗺️

Two Key Areas Compared

Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOCG:
The hills around Jesi, closer to the Adriatic, on limestone + clay: mineral, high-acid and elegant; Riserva aged at least 18 months

Verdicchio di Matelica DOCG:
A higher, more inland north-south valley without maritime influence: more continental with wide day-night swings, a tighter structure, higher acidity and greater ageing potential

The signature bottle: from the 1950s an amphora-shaped bottle became popular; quality-minded producers later mostly switched to conventional bottles

slides.3.title: ⏳ Verdicchio — Three Stages of Ageing
slides.3.content:
Verdicchio's remarkable transformation with age — high acidity is the key to long ageing, and top Matelica Riserva can rival the complexity of great white Burgundy

🍼 Young (1-3 years)

Fresh lemon, green apple, white flowers, herbs; sharp, lively acidity; light and easy; best with: oysters, raw seafood, seafood salad

🍷 Developing (4-8 years)

Ripe citrus, honey, toasted almond, deepening minerality; acidity integrated and balanced; an oily texture begins to appear; best with: grilled fish, white meat, pasta in cream sauce

🏆 Mature (10-20 years)

Beeswax, hazelnut, truffle, wet stone, complex spice; acidity still clear but silky; complexity rivalling top white Burgundy; best with: white truffle dishes, aged cheese

slides.4.title: ⚠️ Montepulciano — Italy's Most Famous Confusion
slides.4.content:
⚠️ One of the most famous confusions in Italian wine — Montepulciano is both a red grape of Abruzzo and a town in Tuscany; the lead grape of Vino Nobile is Sangiovese, not Montepulciano!

🍇 Montepulciano (grape) — Abruzzo

Type: red grape variety

Where: Abruzzo (and other central areas such as Marche)

Traits: deep purple-black (very rich in anthocyanins), medium-high but soft tannins, high acidity

Flavours: black cherry, plum, blackberry, spice, chocolate

Key wines:
Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC (large volumes, approachable)
Montepulciano d'Abruzzo Colline Teramane DOCG (the top tier, in the province of Teramo)
Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo DOC (a deep pink rosé from a short maceration)

🏘️ Montepulciano (place) — a Tuscan Town

Type: a Tuscan town in the province of Siena

❌ Common mistake: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is not made from the Montepulciano grape!

✅ Correct: the main grape is Sangiovese (locally Prugnolo Gentile, 70%+)

Ageing: 2 years (1 in oak); Riserva 3 years

Style: balanced and elegant, high acidity, between Chianti Classico and Brunello

Memory tip: place name + wine name → the grape is Sangiovese; grape name + region name → it is the Montepulciano grape

slides.5.title: 💪 Sagrantino — King of Tannin
slides.5.content:
A rare masterpiece from Montefalco in Umbria — considered one of the most tannic grapes in the world, planted on a small area almost entirely in Montefalco, it needs long ageing

💪 Sagrantino Secco — Dry (DOCG)

Grape: 100% Sagrantino

Tannin: extremely high, among the highest in the world

Colour: deep purple-black (almost opaque)

Alcohol: 14-16%

Ageing rules: about 3 years (at least 12 months in oak)

Flavours: blackberry, dark chocolate, leather, tobacco, spice

Serving tip: very tight and astringent when young; decant or be patient with ageing

🍯 Sagrantino Passito — Sweet

Method: grapes dried for about 2 months (passito) before vinification

Ageing: similar requirements to the dry version

Style: sweet, rich and layered

Flavours: dried fruit, fig, dark chocolate, honey and spice

Historical importance: Sagrantino's original traditional style! The dry Secco only became popular from the 1970s onwards

Pairing: chocolate desserts, blue cheese, dried-fruit pastries

🔬 Why Is the Tannin So High?

Sagrantino's very high tannin comes from very thick skins (a high skin-and-seed ratio) + high polyphenol content (rich in anthocyanins) + long maceration. The name may come from "sagra" (a religious festival); traditionally friars used the sweet passito version as a ceremonial wine.
slides.6.title: 🌊 Vermentino — The Scent of the Mediterranean
slides.6.content:
A white grape of the Mediterranean coast with a clear maritime character — with a distinctive salty minerality and herbal aromas, grown on the coasts of Sardinia, Liguria and Tuscany, a natural partner for seafood

📊 Grape Profile

Acidity: medium to high

Body: medium

Alcohol: 12-14%

Flavours: lemon, green apple, white peach, white flowers, almond, herbs

Character: coastal salinity, a signature salty finish

Drinking window: 1-4 years, best young and fresh

🗺️ Three Regional Styles

Vermentino di Gallura DOCG (Sardinia):
The only DOCG, granite soils + sea winds: very mineral, salty and high in acidity, the most characterful

Vermentino di Sardegna DOC:
The whole island of Sardinia, fresh and easy, lively fruit, relaxed everyday drinking

Colli di Luni DOC (Liguria-Tuscany border):
Intensely herbal, marked minerality and an almond finish, the Ligurian style

🍽️ Its maritime minerality makes Vermentino a natural match for seafood: oysters, clams, mussels, grilled fish, lobster, as well as Liguria's Pesto alla Genovese and Sardinia's bottarga (cured mullet roe)
slides.7.title: 🌾 Trebbiano — Italy's Workhorse
slides.7.content:
One of the most widely planted white grape names in Italy — "Trebbiano" is actually a name shared by several different varieties, with huge differences in quality: from neutral, mass-produced Toscano to the few Abruzzo whites able to age for a long time

⚪ Trebbiano Toscano (= France's Ugni Blanc)

The most widely planted Trebbiano: neutral, high-acid and high-yielding. It was once a required grape in the Chianti blend; in France it is called Ugni Blanc and is the main base wine distilled for Cognac. Its importance in many appellations' rules is declining today.

⭐ Trebbiano d'Abruzzo (the top example)

Trebbiano d'Abruzzo DOC in Abruzzo (the rules also allow varieties such as Bombino Bianco). Most wines are fresh and easy, but a few traditional estates make whites that can age for a long time. Flavours: white peach, apricot, almond, minerality. Producers: Valentini, Emidio Pepe.

⭐ Trebbiano di Soave (= a close relative of Verdicchio)

Used in Veneto's Soave DOC; DNA studies show it is genetically very close to Verdicchio. Style: mineral, almond, high acidity. Proof that not every Trebbiano is ordinary — some members of the family have remarkable ageing potential.

slides.8.title: 🐑 Pecorino — The Revival of an Endangered Grape
slides.8.content:
A white grape named "little sheep" (pecora = sheep), native to Marche/Abruzzo — once almost lost, rediscovered from the 1980s, and now one of Italy's most celebrated white-grape revivals

📊 Grape Profile

Acidity: high

Body: medium to full

Alcohol: 13-14.5%

Flavours: white peach, apricot, tropical fruit, white flowers, spice, minerality

Character: aromatic and complex, ageing potential of 5-8 years

🐑 The name: sheep loved eating these grapes, or because Marche/Abruzzo lay on the traditional transumanza (sheep migration) routes

📜 From Near-Extinction to Revival

Mid-20th century: low-yielding, so farmers replanted with productive varieties and it almost disappeared

1980s: rediscovered and championed by Guido Cocci Grifoni and others in Marche

2000s: quality rose and its reputation grew

2011: Offida Pecorino promoted to DOCG (Marche, 85%+ Pecorino)

Today: widely planted in both Marche and Abruzzo, a model revival of an endangered grape

slides.9.title: 📊 Central Italian Grapes Compared
slides.9.content:
🔍 A Guide to Central Italian Grapes

Central Italy's grapes span three regions — Marche, Abruzzo and Umbria — and each red and white has its own personality. Whites revolve around acidity + minerality; reds are distinguished by structure + ageing potential. The biggest trap: Montepulciano the grape ≠ Montepulciano the town.

⚪ Central Italian Whites (Verdicchio / Vermentino / Pecorino / Trebbiano)

Verdicchio (Marche, ages 10-20 years, mineral like Chablis) ✦ Vermentino (coastal minerality, the seafood choice) ✦ Pecorino (aromatic and complex, a revival story, 5-8 years) ✦ Trebbiano (a family of very uneven quality, top Abruzzo vs ordinary Toscano)

🍇 Central Italian Reds (Montepulciano the grape / Sagrantino)

Montepulciano the grape (purple-black, high anthocyanins, medium-high soft tannins, approachable, with Cerasuolo rosé as a speciality) ✦ Sagrantino (among the most tannic grapes in the world, planted on a small area, needs long ageing)

⚠️ The Central Italian Trap to Remember

Montepulciano (a grape, Abruzzo reds) ≠ Vino Nobile di Montepulciano (a place in Tuscany, made mainly from Sangiovese / Prugnolo Gentile). This is the most common confusion in Italian wine exams, sommelier certifications and real-life wine buying!

slides.10.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.10.points.0: ✓ Verdicchio is Italy's most underrated white grape, high in acid and mineral like "Italy's Chablis", with top wines able to age 10-20 years
slides.10.points.1: ✓ Verdicchio's two DOCGs: Castelli di Jesi (limestone, elegant and mineral) vs Matelica (higher, tighter structure, greater ageing potential)
slides.10.points.2: ✓ Montepulciano's famous confusion: the grape (Abruzzo reds) ≠ the town (in Tuscany, where Vino Nobile is made mainly from Sangiovese / Prugnolo Gentile)
slides.10.points.3: ✓ Montepulciano the grape: purple-black, high anthocyanins, medium-high soft tannins, high acidity; Colline Teramane DOCG is the top tier and Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo a distinctive deep rosé
slides.10.points.4: ✓ Sagrantino is considered one of the most tannic grapes in the world, planted on a small area almost entirely in Montefalco, and needs long ageing
slides.10.points.5: ✓ Sagrantino comes in two styles, the dry Secco (about 3 years of ageing, at least 12 months in oak) and the sweet Passito — the sweet version is the historical, traditional ceremonial wine
slides.10.points.6: ✓ Vermentino is a Mediterranean coastal grape; Vermentino di Gallura DOCG (Sardinia, granite) is the only DOCG, with marked salty minerality, the first choice for seafood
slides.10.points.7: ✓ The Trebbiano family varies hugely in quality: Toscano (= Ugni Blanc, the Cognac base, neutral) vs Abruzzo (a few great estates such as Valentini make long-lived wines)
slides.10.points.8: ✓ Pecorino ("little sheep" grape) almost disappeared and has been revived since the 1980s; Offida Pecorino DOCG (promoted in 2011), aromatic and complex, great value
